---
name: chammi-reformat-test
description: "Real bench test of the chammi-75 reformatting spec: rechunk validated (decode-amp 6->1, 3-8x faster), but one-shard-per-array REGRESSED throughput ~25% on the fast mount"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 7acaf5cf-43e7-4554-bbec-35f2521d300f
---

Tested the `reformatting-spec.md` recommendations on real chammi-75 data (2026-06-15,
cold-cache L40, 512 arrays / 3200 samples each). Built a controlled A/B/C and benched.

**Tooling (cluster-side, with the survey tooling in `~/data/damacy/scenarios/`):**
- `make_sharded_chammi.py` — tensorstore writer: reads each original FOV level-0 array,
  writes a zarr-v3 copy with inner chunk `[1,1,1,256,256]`, **one shard per array**
  (sharding_indexed, shard shape = whole array, so 128 inner chunks -> 1 file), zstd-3,
  crc32c index. Takes a "before" scenario, emits the matched "after" scenario.
- Scenarios in `~/data/damacy/scenarios/chammi/`: `before-mix`/`after-mix` (512 arrays
  across ~50 studies, the spec-mix baseline) and the idr0017 triple `before-idr0017`
  (whole-plane chunk) / `ivirshup-idr0017` (ivirshup's 256^2 chunks, UNSHARDED, 128
  files/array) / `after-idr0017` (my 256^2 SHARDED, 1 file/array). All three of the triple
  are identical except `store_root` (same uris/sampling/pipeline) — sharding is the only
  variable. Sharded data: `~/data/damacy/chammi-sharded/{mix,idr0017}` (~3 GB).
- Built from `katamari_to_scenario.py --limit 512` over `CHAMMI-75/train.csv` (2.37M
  distinct FOV arrays). damacy reads the sharded zarr-v3 (sharding_indexed+zstd+crc32c) fine.

**Finding 1 — the rechunk is the win, exactly as the what-if predicted.** decode-amp
collapses `before 5.94x -> after 0.99x` (mix) and `16.0x -> 0.99x` (idr0017); spec what-if
said chammi `6.2 -> 1.0x`. Bound flips decode->io. Throughput: mix `0.24 -> 0.82 GB/s`
(3.4x), idr0017 `0.21 -> 1.79 GB/s` (8.5x, to the unsharded rechunk). The inner chunk shape
is the whole story, and **ivirshup's existing rechunk already captures it** (it applied the
256^2 chunk but did NOT shard — 128 files/array).

**Finding 2 — sharding REGRESSED throughput ~25% on the fast mount (the surprise).** idr0017
triple isolates it (io-amp identical 0.51x both — same bytes; only file layout differs):
unsharded (128 files/arr) **1.79 GB/s** vs one-shard-per-array **1.35 GB/s**. Mechanism: on
`/mnt/main0` (nconnect=16) damacy's read pool feeds on INDEPENDENT FILES; ~12k separate chunk
files keep the 64-thread pool perfectly overlapped (wire 0.92 GB/s), while 508 shards
concentrate reads on fewer files + add a shard-index read dependency + within-shard
contention (wire 0.69 GB/s). Sharded did HALF the reads and 20x fewer statx (536 vs 11,428)
yet MORE io_ms (949 vs 566). So the user's "~64 shards for read parallelism" worry points the
opposite way here: **more files = more parallelism**; 508 shards already clears the 64-deep
pool, consolidating further just removes work the pool wanted.

**So the spec's "small chunks MUST be sharded or you trade decode waste for a file-count
explosion" is too absolute.** On the fast training mount the file-count explosion is what the
read pool likes. Sharding's real justification is what this throughput bench does NOT capture:
(1) corpus-scale inode pressure (2.37M FOVs x 128 files ~ 300M tiny files), (2) slow /
object-store mounts (single-stream runai NFS, S3) where per-file open/GET latency dominates and
fewer-bigger-reads would flip to a win. Recommend: rechunk unconditionally; treat
one-shard-per-array as mount/scale-dependent, not mandatory.

**Shard-granularity sweep -> LANDING RECOMMENDATION: target >=16 shards/array (2026-06-15,
idr0017).** Swept shards/array 1,2,4,8,16,32,64,128 (sharding_indexed) + unsharded(128 ref), all
via `make_sharded_chammi.py --shard-chunks T,C,Z,Y,X` (inner chunks per shard; Y-then-X-then-C
tiling, e.g. `1,2,1,1,4`->16 shards), 120 batches x 3 cold repeats, one back-to-back GPU job.
Iterated readings (each denser look revised the last): 50-batch single run -> spurious "4-shard
peak" (NOISE, sub-second walls); sparse 1/4/8/128 -> looked "monotonic, unsharded best"; dense
1..128 -> apparent hump peaking ~32. **Resolution (user's call, sound): the MEAN is contention-
noisy (other tenants load the shared NFS), so the MAX over repeats — the uncontended ceiling — is
the meaningful number, and the MAX SATURATES AT 16 shards/array** (max GB/s: 1->1.07, 2->1.54,
4->1.34, 8->1.84, **16->2.05**, 32->2.22[lucky], 64->2.01, 128->1.96). **16 = the mount's
nconnect=16** (TCP connections per NFS mount): once an array is spread over >=16 independent shard
files the read pool saturates all 16 connections; more shards add no wire parallelism, so the
ceiling flattens exactly there. A predictive mechanism, not a fit. **>=16 shards/array also hits
the full unsharded ceiling at 8x FEWER files** (16 vs 128/array) -> satisfies throughput AND the
file-count concern that motivates sharding. For chammi's 128-inner-chunk arrays that's ~8
chunks/shard (e.g. shard `[1,2,1,256,1024]`). One-shard-per-array (the spec's "small array"
default) is the WORST rechunked layout (~half the ceiling). **General rule: shards/array >= the
mount's read-parallelism width (NFS nconnect); 16 for /mnt/main0.** Still-open: slow runai PVC / S3
(per-file open latency may shift the elbow). Confirm scenarios + sweep/fit parsers in
`~/tmp/2026-06-15-chammi-reformat/`.
See [[corpus-survey]], [[reformatting-spec]] (in damacy-slides repo), [[throughput-bench]], [[array-starve-154]].

---
name: corpus-survey
description: "Lightweight katamari-corpus throughput survey harness + finding that MIP datasets are read-amplification-bound, not mount-bound"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 7421e381-c175-4c55-b625-af782270afb8
---

Lightweight survey of damacy throughput across katamari training datasets
(2026-06-12). Harness lives in `~/data/damacy/scenarios/` next to the dynacell
converter: `survey.py` holds a DATASETS table (manifest CSV + patch shape, taken
from `production_v1.yaml`'s per-dataset `sample_shape`) and drives
`katamari_to_scenario.py` then `bench/run.py`, emitting one table.
`uv run survey.py --gen-only` is login-safe; plain `uv run survey.py` needs a GPU
(L40 is fine — IO-bound). `--preset baseline|tuned`, `--limit N` (default 512).

**Converter upgrades (this session, in `katamari_to_scenario.py`):** `--limit`
(string-only dedup pass first, then random-sample N distinct arrays before
stat-ing — CHAMMI's manifest is 2.4M rows); `--n-io-threads`; auto-sizes
`n_shard_index_cache` to the `(lookahead+2*spb)*64` floor damacy now enforces;
and **auto-sizes `max_chunk_uncompressed_mb` to the dataset's largest decode
chunk** (parses each array's zarr.json) — `--max-chunk-mb` is now just a floor.

**Production trains on the MIP (2D) manifest variants, not the raw 3D arrays.**
`production_v1.yaml` maps jacobo→`jacobo_mip`, allencell-dynamic→
`allencell-dynamic-nuc-morph_mip`, allencell-static→`allencell-static-hipsc-fov_mip`;
CHAMMI-75 is already 2D. All four live on **fast `/mnt/main0`** (`/bio` symlink);
the slow runai PVC only holds the raw 3D variants production doesn't use. Patches
are tiny single-channel 2D crops: static `[1,1,1,256,256]`, video `[16,1,1,256,256]`.

**Headline finding: all four are DECODE-bound (decode stage = 99–100% of wall),
NOT mount- or GPU-bound, and the dynacell tuning preset (n_io_threads=64 + 4MB
coalesce) does nothing here (tuned == baseline).** Cold-cache L40, 512 arrays/ds:
allencell_static 0.39 GB/s (1669 samp/s), chammi75 0.25 (1056), jacobo_mip 0.21
(56), allencell_dynamic 0.14 (38, only 2 train arrays total). A 256×256 patch
forces decoding the **whole declared chunk** — arrays are unsharded with coarse
chunks (12 MiB CHAMMI / 32 MiB allencell / up to 184 MiB jacobo), often one chunk
per channel/array. **The meaningful metric is decode amplification (uncompressed
chunk volume decoded ÷ patch bytes), not io amplification.** io_amp looks mild
(2.4–19x) because the unused chunk volume compresses to ~nothing on disk, but it
still expands on decode: allencell_static io_amp 2.4x BUT **dec_amp 116x** (decodes
107 GB to deliver 0.92 GB of patches). Cleanest example: allencell_static declared
chunk `[16,1,1,1024,1024]` uint16 = 32 MiB nominal vs array `[1,7,1,624,924]` —
over-declares T 16x (array T=1) and is 1024² spatially vs the 256² patch. **Lever
is chunk geometry, not IO tuning.** NOTE: you MUST decode the full nominal chunk —
blosc/zstd compress the whole chunk as a unit, so partial/sub-chunk decode is
impossible (damacy already does chunk *skipping*: allencell touches 1 of 7
channel-chunks). The 107 GB is intrinsic to the chunking. Real fix = re-chunk
(offline). **Phrasing the user cares about (2026-06-13): the principle is NOT "match
the chunk to how it's read." It's "chunks small, and small in the right way":**
(a) chunk smaller than the patch — under 1 MB, tolerable down to ~64 kB (below that
compression suffers); the problem we see is chunks about the same size as or larger
than the patch. (b) give a dimension a chunk extent > 1 ONLY where neighboring values
correlate enough to compress together — x and y always, time sometimes, depth
sometimes, channels rarely; an extent the patch reads only a slice of (e.g. the
allencell T=16 over a T=1 array, or a z-extent a 2D crop ignores) is wasted on every
read. (Decoded-chunk reuse cache was considered and rejected — see below.) decode is
bound by output volume materialization
(allencell_static 107 GB @ 51 GB/s_out = the wall) — codec speed is NOT the limit
(51 GB/s ÷ decode_amp 116 = 0.44 ≈ measured 0.4 GB/s).

**Reformatting plan + what-if (2026-06-13):** `dev/reformatting-spec.md` in the repo
(PR #158) is the draft plan; `rechunk_whatif.py` (cluster-side, with the survey
tooling) predicts decode waste for any proposed chunk shape vs real array+patch (no
GPU; reproduces measured befores). Computed targets (chunk `[1,1,1,256,256]` for
static/video, `[1,1,4,256,256]` for 3D-z-range): allencell_nuclear 131→1.9x,
allencell_static 128→2.0x, dynacell_mip 33→4x, jacobo_mip 31→4x, nucmorph/emt 22→2x,
cellstate 9→4x, chammi 6.2→1x, liberali_ls1 6.1→2x. **Correction on the raw 3D
variants:** their scary 76–163x is a 2D-crop-on-3D-data ARTIFACT (reading 1 z from a
whole-z chunk); read with a proper z-range crop the current raw chunks are only
~5–10x, and target `[1,1,4,256,256]` gives ~2–5x (jacobo raw 10.2→4.7, allencell raw
4.6→2.4). So the raw-3D move is "use a z-range crop (most of it) + small z-extent
chunks like raw dynacell already has." Findings: spatial=crop not bigger (512²
doubles waste); t=1 beats t>1 on read waste (t-extent only earns its place via a
compression gain); raw dynacell `[1,1,4,256,256]` is the template to copy.
**Shard size (user's standing rec, keep consistent): ~1 GB uncompressed or larger.**
The "maximum shard size" question that confuses people is better framed as a
file-count floor, NOT a byte ceiling: a shard is the unit of parallel-read
independence (damacy interleaves reads across shards), so the in-flight read window
must span enough independent files (shards + arrays) to fill the read pool (dozens).
Large arrays → 1 GB shards give dozens/array automatically; small arrays (<1 GB) are
one shard each, parallelism is cross-array; danger zone = few arrays AND few shards
([[corpus-survey]] #154). dynacell shards ~1–2 GB uncompressed, dozens/array.

**Reuse quantified (`reuse_analysis.py`, analytic, validated vs measured):** the
~1.5x I first quoted was a 50-batch artifact — at 3200 patches allencell_static
hasn't even touched all its distinct chunks. Replaying the sampler against real
chunk grids: dec_amp_nocache reproduces measured (allencell_static 128 vs 116,
jacobo 31 vs 28, chammi 5.9 vs 5.4, dynamic 22 vs 20). With a perfect pre-decode
cache, dec_amp collapses once patches drawn > distinct chunks: allencell_static
128→78 (3.2k patches) →7.7 (51k) →1.9 (205k); the others fall below 1x by ~12k.
**Distinct-chunk working sets: chammi ~2 GB, dynamic ~18 GB (fit in GPU),
allencell_static ~96 GB, jacobo ~106 GB (need host RAM).** Practical constraints:
(1) under shuffled epoch sampling a chunk is revisited only after all ~3000
others, so the cache must be ~working-set-sized to capture reuse (small LRU
mostly misses); (2) drive dec_amp→1 and the bottleneck reverts to io/transfer
(cold ~2–5 GB/s), NOT 51 — so caching lifts allencell_static 0.4 → a few GB/s,
back into the IO-tuning regime. So at fixed chunking, GPU-decode's edge only
matters on cold/uncached passes; warm, decode amortizes to ~free on CPU or GPU.

**Corpus-wide characterization (2026-06-13, `corpus_scan.py` → `corpus/report.md`
+ summary.json):** metadata-only scan (no GPU/bench) over production_v2 (32
datasets) + 7 raw 3D variants, computing predicted decode_amp from chunk geometry
vs each dataset's training patch. Self-check reproduced the 4 benchmarked values.
**0 ozx-flagged / 0 unavailable** — v2 routes rxrx/lincs/cellpaint to readable
`data_uncompressed/` dirs, not the .ozx zip stores. **Most of the corpus is already
well-formed: 23/32 at decode_amp ≲5 (sharded ~0.5 MiB chunks — that group IS the
target template).** Decode-bound problem concentrated in ~9 datasets, two regimes:
over-declared-fill (allencell_nuclear 131x, allencell_static 128x — 32 MiB UNSHARDED
chunks [16,1,1,1024,1024] over ~[1,7,1,624,924] arrays, fill 0.01-0.03) and unsharded
coarse MIP timelapses (dynacell 33x, jacobo_mip 31x, nucmorph 22x, emt 22x — 32-64
MiB unsharded vs 4 MiB patch). Regimes: well-formed 23, coarse-chunk 6, unsharded-
many-files 6, over-declared-fill 4. Two model-corrections: (1) **the production
"dynacell" = the MIP variant (64 MiB unsharded, 33x, decode-bound), NOT the raw 5D
sharded-1MiB dynacell I tuned (4.3x, IO-bound)** — different data+patch; "dynacell is
the good control" only describes the raw-sharded path. (2) **decode_amp depends on
the PATCH as much as the chunk**: even well-sharded raw dynacell is 15.9x at the
16-frame 2D video patch (fans out over 16 T-chunks + 2x2 spatial straddle). So a
format spec must match chunk geometry to the patch (temporal chunking to read-T,
spatial alignment), not just "small chunks". Raw 3D variants uniformly bad for
current patches (jacobo raw 163x, emt/nucmorph/liberali ~140x) → the move to raw
3D + z-range needs reformatting first. corpus_scan.py reusable for the spec work.

**tensorstore CPU-decode comparison (issue #153, `tensorstore_bench.py`):** built
to A/B damacy (GPU) vs tensorstore (CPU-only, the leading CPU zarr reader) on the
SAME data/chunking/patches. Ports bench/main.c's xorshift64* RNG so patch
positions match damacy bit-for-bit; sweeps tensorstore thread count (the real
competitor to one GPU decode stream); `--drop-cache` mirrors run.py. Smoke-tested;
full cold sweep is a CPU-node srun (see issue). Decision context: tensorstore is
the CPU-only option; damacy's GPU decode wins mainly on cold/uncached decode. Caveat: survey
samples uniformly at random; the real loader's patch cache + `sample_overlap`
amortize over-decode, so real-training amplification is likely lower — worth
measuring. survey.py now reports io_amp, dec_amp, and bound stage. Full table in
`~/data/damacy/scenarios/survey/FINDINGS.md`. See [[dynacell-benchmark]],
[[throughput-bench]], [[io-bottleneck-investigation]].

---
name: katamari-real-crop
description: "Katamari's REAL training crop is 128x128 single-channel (1 MiB), not the 20 MiB [1,5,16,256,256] the damacy benches used — corrects samples/s and the reformatting targets"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: bf3331be-0d2f-43f7-a29d-9c4e79691407
---

Found 2026-06-15 while sourcing dynacell samples/s. **The damacy throughput benches
used the wrong sample shape.** Array-starve / tensorstore comparison (the 4.49–4.85 GB/s
dynacell lineage) sampled `[1,5,16,256,256]` f32 = **20 MiB** (5 channels stacked, 256²).

**Katamari never does that.** Loader is at `~/src/evolutionaryscale/projects/katamari`;
crop is set by `sample_shape` in `configs/data/*.yaml`, NOT in the manifests (manifests
carry only path/resolution/time_range/channels). `auto_split_by_channels: true` makes
every sample **c=1**; data is MIP so **z=1**. dynacell uses the video-16 anchor →
`[16,1,1,128,128]` f32 = **1 MiB** (channels [3,4,5] after `exclude_channels:[0,1]`).

Sample sizes vary by dataset, only on T and spatial (c,z always 1):
- base config `combined_2d_video_multichannel` (exp `..._2d_video.yaml`) = **128²**:
  video-16 `[16,1,1,128,128]` 1 MiB; video-3 192 KiB; static `[1,1,1,128,128]` 64 KiB.
- variant `..._256` (exp `..._2d_video_v2.yaml`) = **256²**: `[16,1,1,256,256]` 4 MiB etc.
  (the "v1/v2" naming is just my shorthand for the two experiment files, not official.)

**Consequence for samples/s:** at 4.85 GB/s output, dynacell ≈ **4,625 samp/s** at 1 MiB
(128²) or 1,156 at 4 MiB (256²) — NOT the ~235 samp/s the 20 MiB bench implied. The
storage ceiling (~16.5 GB/s, 16-conn O_DIRECT replay) and the wire=output×amplification
relation are crop-independent, but the 2.80× read amplification was measured on the 20 MiB
crop and does NOT transfer to 128².

**Consequence for reformatting ([[chammi-reformat-test]], [[corpus-survey]],
reformatting-spec.md/optimization.md in damacy-slides-2026-06):** all decode-waste numbers
were computed at 256² crops. At the real 128² crop a crop needs 4× fewer bytes against the
same chunks, so **every "before" decode-waste is ~4× higher** (dynacell-MIP 33→135×,
allencell-static 128→512×) and the **target inner chunk must be 128² not 256²** — a 256²
chunk on a 128² crop is 4× the crop area and ~doubles the residual (dynacell 4.0→8.4×).
New target rule: spatial = crop (128); pad **t** to clear the 64 KiB floor on narrow-dtype
video (u16→t=2, u8→t=4; ~+0.1× waste since a 16-frame crop reads the whole t extent);
static narrow-dtype (T=1) is stuck sub-floor (u16 32 KiB, u8 16 KiB) — accept + verify
compression. Recompute via `~/data/damacy/scenarios/rechunk_whatif.py` (pure geometry).

**Full-corpus re-scan done (`corpus_scan.py`, metadata-only, both crops,
`~/tmp/2026-06-15-corpus128/{corpus,corpus256}`).** corpus_scan reads the EXISTING chunk
only — it does NOT model t-padded/candidate chunks (that's rechunk_whatif). Well-formed
(decode amp ≤6×): **23 @256² → 11 @128²**; needs-reformatting **9 → 21** of 32. The 256²
scan reproduces the original 23/9, confirming the method. Twelve datasets cross ✓→✗ at
128² (chunks ~256² spatial): rxrx2/19a/19b, lincs, periscope, hpa_v25, 4i_nascentrna
×2, cellstate_tracking, c2c12_cell_tracks, evican, liberali_ls2_mip. Well-formed at both:
chad_actin, NIST, rxrx1, idr0002, erk, alfi, biad2515, opencell, livecell, cellpaint_posh,
cbvcc. Both slides docs now carry a dual-crop (256² vs 128²) per-dataset characterization
table. **Compression survey DONE** (`~/tmp/2026-06-15-compression-survey/`, CPU node, real
recompress at target chunks with each store's own codec, bootstrap CI): sub-floor static
chunks compress fine — **u16 @32 KiB loses ~0% vs current (allencell_static/nuclear
2.0×/2.3×), u8 @16 KiB a few % (rxrx, chammi)**, nothing incompressible. 64 KiB floor is
soft, not a cliff. GOTCHA: per-block ratios are heavy-tailed (empty tiles compress
100–3000×) so the survey's MEAN column is inflated (lincs/periscope mean ~150–300× but
median ~1.4×) — use median or a size-weighted aggregate, not the mean.

**On-disk size impact DONE** (`~/tmp/2026-06-15-size-impact/`, CPU node, size-weighted
aggregate ratio Σcomp_target/Σcomp_current, `du`-anchored to real on-disk bytes within a
few % on 30/36): reformatting to the 128² targets is **size-neutral — corpus-weighted
size_ratio ≈ 1.00 (~65.5 TiB→65.5 TiB), every dataset within ±5.5%** (5 shrink ~4%, 5 grow
≤5.5%, rest ±2%). It's a decode/IO win, NOT a storage cost (re-tiles same pixels;
over-declared fill already compresses away). Only real grower = arrays smaller than 128²
(cbvcc 50×50, +5%, edge-fill padding). Sharded stores' size_ratio_real column is unreliable
(shard-index overhead unmodeled) but the modeled same-data size_ratio is robust. Both slides
docs updated.

**damacy GPU throughput measured at 128² crop, current un-reformatted stores** (H100,
tuned preset n_io_threads=64/read-op 4MB, `~/tmp/2026-06-15-bench128/`): chammi75 **0.05
GB/s** (decode-bound 100%, decodes 3.2→5.0 GB), allencell-static **0.08 GB/s** (decode-bound
100%, decodes 2.2→**107 GB** ≈478× waste), dynacell-raw-sharded **0.47 GB/s** (IO-bound, wire
10.5 GB/s near the ~16.5 ceiling, read-amp 22×). **dynacell-MIP is UNREADABLE by damacy**: its
64 MiB *blosc* chunk exceeds `DAMACY_BLOSC_MAX_CHUNK_UNCOMPRESSED_BYTES`=16 MB
(`src/damacy_limits.h:93`, enforced `zarr/zarr_chunk_layout.c:44`) → DAMACY_DECODE regardless of
the config `max_chunk_uncompressed_mb`. (allencell-static's 32 MiB chunk benches fine because
it's zstd, not blosc — the 16 MB cap is blosc1-decoder-specific.) Key result: at the real 128²
crop EVERY current store performs badly — even the well-chunked raw dynacell tanks to 0.47 GB/s
(from 4.49 at 256²) because its 256²-spatial chunk dwarfs the 128² crop (22× read-amp). Strong
reformatting motivation: MIP isn't just slow, it's unreadable.

**Reformatted-dynacell bench (`~/tmp/2026-06-15-dynacell-reformat/`, H100, 128² crop, same
50 arrays, A/B by inner chunk, same blosc codec):** rechunk `[1,1,4,256,256]`→`[1,1,1,128,128]`
(32 shards/array) drops **read amplification 20.7×→3.3×** (6.2× less io: 69.5→11.2 GB),
throughput 1.04→**1.43 GB/s** on the matched window (1.4×), samples/s 1097→1504. **Bottleneck
stays IO** (decode_gap 71% = GPU idles on reads; decode never limits). Matches the spec's
~2-4× residual prediction. Caveat: source arrays are 45-78 GB each (~3 TB), so benched a
bounded window `[16,1,8,512,512]`/array, not full extents — read-amp drop is regime-invariant
and trustworthy; full-cold throughput gain likely >1.4× but unmeasured. See
[[dynacell-benchmark]], [[katamari-loader-overlap]], [[io-bottleneck-investigation]].
